transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I suppose I’ve just been feeling like I can’t quite settle. For the past year or so, I’m always puttering around—fixing something, arranging things, saying yes to one more little volunteer thing. Even at my age, I have a hard time just sitting still.
Do you often feel anxious or worried?
I wouldn’t say anxious, exactly. I mean, I worry about the usual things now and then, but it’s not what I’d call the main problem.
Do you find yourself often taking on more activities or tasks than you can handle?

Yes… I suppose I do. I’m always saying I’ll just help with one more thing, or fix up one more little project, and then I’ve got more going on than I meant to. It’s hard for me to just sit down and leave things alone.
Do you feel unhappy or irritable when you're not actively doing something?
A little, yes. I don’t know if I’d call it unhappy… but I get restless when I’m not doing something. I tend to start puttering around or fixing things, just to keep moving.
Do you feel overwhelmed or stressed by your constant need to be active?

Yes… maybe a bit stressed, mostly because I can’t seem to just sit. This past year I’m always puttering around, fixing something, arranging things, or agreeing to one more little thing. Even at my age, being still is hard.
Do you feel sad or empty often?
No… not often, I don’t think. I have my moods, like anyone, but I wouldn’t say sad or empty most of the time.
Do you often feel tired?
Not especially… I mean, I’m 87, so I do get tired sometimes. But I haven’t really noticed it as a big problem.
Has your constant need to be active interfered with your relationships or daily life in a significant way?

A little, yes. At the senior center, I’ve had to apologize after meetings sometimes. One friend even said maybe I should take a smaller role at the sign-up table, because I was… making things a bit tense.
Do you often talk more than others in social situations?
I don’t really know. I suppose I can, sometimes… but I haven’t paid close attention to whether it’s more than other people.
Do you often find yourself dominating conversations?
I’m not sure I’d say “dominating.” I might talk a bit much at times, but I don’t always notice it while it’s happening.
Do you have trouble waiting for your turn in line or in conversations?

Yes… sometimes. Waiting in the sign-up line, or when supplies are being handed out, I get a bit fidgety. I’ll catch myself sighing or looking at my watch, maybe inching forward when I should just stay put.
Do you think your constant activity and restlessness are causing problems for you?

Yes… I suppose it has, a little. At the senior center, I’ve had to apologize after meetings. And one friend said maybe I should take a smaller role at the sign-up table, because… well, my manner was making people tense.
Do you think you act this way to get attention from others?
I don’t think so… not really. I’m not trying to get attention. It just sort of happens before I think about it.
Do you think you would still feel the need to be constantly active if you were alone?
Yes… I think I would. Even when I’m by myself, I tend to be puttering around—fixing little things, arranging this or that. It’s hard for me to just sit still, even now.
Do you think you would be less active or restless if you were in a quieter, less social environment?
Maybe a little, but… I don’t think it would go away. Even somewhere quiet, I’d still find myself puttering around, fixing or arranging things. I just have a hard time sitting still.
Do you think you would be less active or restless around other people if they didn't interact with you or pay attention to you?

I don’t think attention from people makes much difference. I’m just… always doing something lately—puttering, fixing things, arranging things. Even if no one’s paying me any mind, I still have trouble just sitting still.
Do you think you would be as active and restless if you were living completely alone with no social interactions?

Yes… I think so. Even if I were completely alone, I’d still be puttering around, fixing or arranging things. That’s sort of what brought me in—this past year or so, I just have a hard time sitting down and being still.
Do you think you would be more likely to engage in these activities if you were doing them with other people?

Maybe a little, if someone asked me to help with something. But it’s not really about other people. I’m like that on my own too—puttering, fixing things, arranging things… volunteering for one more thing. I just don’t sit still very well lately.
Do you think you would be less restless if you were doing these activities completely on your own?

No… I don’t think being on my own would change it much. It’s more that I just keep puttering or fixing things, arranging something, taking on one more little task. Even at my age, I have trouble just sitting down and being still.
Do you think you would be as active and restless if you had no opportunities to interact with others?

Yes, I think so. Even without people around, I’d still be doing little things—puttering, fixing, arranging. That’s really why I came in… this past year I just haven’t been able to sit still very well, even at 87.
